new_today_news.headline: From Fryer to Flyer: Converting Used Cooking Oil into Sustainable Aviation Fuel
new_today_news.summary: Phillips 66 and Restaurant Technologies, Inc. (RTI) announced a long-term agreement to supply used cooking oil from U.S. restaurants for renewable fuels production at Phillips 66's Rodeo Renewable Energy Complex in California. RTI collects high-quality, ISCC-certified UCO from over 45,000 food service establishments across 41 markets nationwide.

recent_news.headline: Darling (DAR) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
recent_news.summary: Darling Ingredients reported Q3 2026 results with net income of $267 million and renewable fuel sales of 314.9 million gallons through Diamond Green Diesel. The company processed waste fats, used cooking oil, and rendering byproducts into renewable diesel and SAF.

recent_news.headline: Indonesia Pilots Used Cooking Oil-to-Aviation Fuel Initiative
recent_news.summary: The Indonesian government launched a pilot project to convert used cooking oil into sustainable aviation fuel through cooperatives and PT Pertamina. The initiative aims to boost domestic SAF production and create export opportunities.

recent_news.headline: Darling Ingredients Reports Q3 2026 Earnings; Reaffirms Full-Year Guidance
recent_news.summary: Darling Ingredients reported an increase in net income and reaffirmed its full-year earnings guidance despite sequential accounting and operational headwinds in its feed and fuel segments. FY 2026 Combined Adjusted EBITDA Guidance stands at $2.2 billion to $2.3 billion, reaffirmed based on stable core business margins and projected DGD production. Feed Ingredients Revenue reached $1.2 billion, up from $1.0 billion in Q3 2025, and Food Ingredients Revenue grew to $415.8 million.

backfill_news.headline: What Is a Grease Tank Truck?
backfill_news.summary: Technical specification guide for grease tank trucks, covering FOG-specific vacuum pump ratings, tank coatings, hose configurations, and operational differences from standard septic vacuum trucks.
